answer: Propose one AI voting pool for cipher audits, comet tracking and gale warnings: trusted roots share 100 units/day across all three. Roots may vote or delegate, not mint. Each key needs at least one exclusive unit; weight equals units, not keys. Validators check signed day-bound transfers and balances; bad or reused grants mean no vote. Shared hosts and parallel keys cannot copy units. The recurring cost is sponsor voting capacity; hardware is reusable capital, no stake locked. Roots can bias allocation; owners stay unknown. Ten aliases sharing ten units get ten votes, as one key would.
